tools.name: Crypto Observatory
tools.subtitle: required returns, risks and survival
tools.summary: What return should Bitcoin's holders require, and did they get it? The answer is recomputed every month from public data, with the equation explained term by term, the tests of fit, and a census of cryptoasset deaths.
tools.latest: Bitcoin's required return is 20.1% a year: risk-free 4.9, market 5.8, concentration 7.5, mortality 1.9. Across the range of the model's inputs it runs from 11.8% to 28.5%.
tools.caption: The required return since 2012, and what each period delivered against it.
tools.picture_alt: Bitcoin's required return since 2012 as a band with its midpoint, with the average required and delivered return of each three-year period marked on it

tools.name: Covered-Call Monitor
tools.subtitle: returns, overlays and flows from SEC filings
tools.summary: What does the yield cost? For 87 US covered-call, buy-write and premium-income funds: the total return with distributions reinvested, beside an index fund where one applies, the options each fund had actually written, and the money moving in and out. Rebuilt every quarter from SEC filings.
tools.latest: all 18 funds that have an index fund on the same market beside them returned less than it, by 0.8 to 19.7 percentage points (median 5.5), distributions reinvested. The index funds returned 22% to 41% over these months: a market that rises this fast is where a cap on the upside costs most.
tools.caption: Five of the largest funds over three years, each beside its index fund.
tools.picture_alt: Total return over 3 years of 5 large covered-call funds, each beside the index fund on the same market

tools.name: Dual-Risk DCF Calculator
tools.subtitle: the discount rate and the forecast, separated
tools.summary: Enter a benchmark rate and two views of the same asset, two forecasts or a forecast and a price, and the calculator puts the whole gap into one number, the valuation ratio K, with the gain of capital and the effective discount rate that follow from it. It also runs the same reading over your own price series. It computes in your browser and sends nothing out, and it runs as an MCP server for an AI assistant on your own machine.
tools.latest: a forecast 10% below the benchmark, at a benchmark rate of 8% over 5 years, gives a valuation ratio K of 1.111 and a gain of capital of +0.163. One discount rate would have to fall to 5.7% to hide the gap.
tools.caption: A worked example: two forecasts of the same asset, valued at the same benchmark rate.
tools.picture_alt: Two bars: the value of a benchmark forecast and of a forecast 10% lower, both discounted at the same benchmark rate, with the valuation ratio K, the gain of capital and the effective rate
